html:
SMTO-EXE-0089 — The area SMTO tried to capture doesn't fit on one screen

GUID: 6231f4ab-1b6b-5b36-8c89-0eddff1fa66b
Slug: screen-invalid-region
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to capture an area that goes past the edge of a screen, or a window that stretches across two monitors. SMTO only captures areas that sit fully on one screen, so nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the window is stretched across two monitors, move it so it sits fully on one monitor, then ask SMTO again. SMTO can only capture a window that fits inside a single screen.
  2. If you asked for a specific part of the screen, ask for a smaller area that stays inside one screen, or for the whole screen instead. An area that crosses a screen's edge can't be captured as one picture.
  3. If you need content from several monitors, ask SMTO to capture each screen separately. Separate captures let SMTO cover every monitor without crossing a screen edge.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns a screenshot of the window or area you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with how your monitors are arranged, to the person who manages that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested rectangle is not fully contained in the selected display, or a window's bounds do not fit inside any single display, so pixel_bounds rejected it.

What this means

  • The requested rectangle was not contained within the selected display, or a window's bounds could not be mapped to one supported display region. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The requested rectangle was not contained within the selected display, or a window's bounds could not be mapped to one supported display region.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact bounds and coordinate space with current display geometry, especially windows spanning displays.

How to fix it

  • Request a region with positive integer dimensions fully contained in one display's bounds, in that display's reported coordinate_space (desktop_physical_pixels on Windows/X11, desktop_points on macOS). For a window spanning displays, capture separate display regions explicitly.
  • Use positive dimensions fully contained in one selected display in its reported coordinate_space. For a window spanning displays, explicitly capture separate display regions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use positive dimensions fully contained in one selected display in its reported coordinate_space. For a window spanning displays, explicitly capture separate display regions.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid contained rectangle maps to the expected pixel bounds on its chosen display.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
